text:
Maya (CEO): Hey team — following the all-hands, open thread for follow-ups on mission/positioning. Drop short Qs and we'll reply throughout the day. TL;DR: focus on predictable, economical inference across deployment modes. :sparkles:

Priya (Head of Product): Quick Q — 'predictable, economical' as product north star: does that mean we deprioritize bleeding-edge model features?

Maya (CEO): Not deprioritize — we evaluate through the lens of production economics. If a model feature increases latency/cost and doesn't move business metrics, it's lower priority. Example: advanced sampling for novelty > useful for some apps, not for transactions.

Kevin (Eng): How do we talk about competitors who advertise 'same-day model upgrades' vs our 'unified runtime'?

Jon (CTO): Emphasize where customers actually fail: unpredictable latency/cost, lack of observability. Our messaging: 'same API, predictable SLOs, cost controls.' Use concrete examples in demos.

Laura (Sales): Can we get a 1-liner for enterprise decks that calls out Private + KMS + SLA?

Maya (CEO): Yes. Suggested: "Redwood Inference — unified inference runtime with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, enterprise SLAs, and KMS integrations." Feel free to shorten.

Sam (Growth): Are there specific customer signals that should trigger outreach to sales (for Dedicated/Private)?

Priya (Head of Product): We defined triggers in last sprint: >$5k/mo usage, 95th p90 latency > 1s, requests with regulated PII. Those are starting points.

Kevin (Eng): Roadmap trade-off: do we prioritize latency optimizations or rollout tooling this quarter?

Maya (CEO): Both are important; prioritize latency infra for high-throughput customers (Dedicated) and rollout tooling for PLG velocity. Triage by customer impact.

Jon (CTO): For messaging to devs: include performance numbers (e.g., multi-tenant median latency, cost per token) in docs. Customers trust numbers.

Priya (Head of Product): Small ask — can we publish the "what winning looks like" metrics in Confluence? Short list.

Maya (CEO): Will do. I'll ask @Priya to draft, @Jon to add numbers. :thumbsup: 

OpsBot: Slides from today's all-hands uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/2026-03-23

Laura (Sales): Any recommended objection handling vs X competitor (emphasizes 'model zoo')?

Maya (CEO): Acknowledge model choice matters. Pivot: emphasize the operational gap — model zoo + poor inference stack = ephemeral wins. Our close: 'we make models reliably cheap and fast in production.'

Kevin (Eng): Quick technical example to use in demos?

Jon (CTO): Use this snippet to show routing fallback:
```
policy:
  - prefer: low_latency
  - fallback: quantized_variant
```
Works well in demo scripts.

Sam (Growth): Will marketing update website messaging this week?

Maya (CEO): Yes — coordinating with design. Expect drafts by EOD Friday.

Priya (Head of Product): Anyone else with follow-ups? If not, I'll collect threads and produce a short actions doc.

Kevin (Eng): +1, I'll add latency numbers to the doc.

Laura (Sales): I'll add enterprise examples.

Maya (CEO): Thanks all. Keep questions here or ping me directly. :heart:
